$comment: The public-surface gate's axes for @cosyte/dicom, read by cosyte-internal-refs (@cosyte/script-utils). Keys starting with $ are notes. Item ids, phase and wave language, plan and roadmap citations, ADR numbers and meta-repo paths belong in the changeset, the changelog, the commit and the pull request, never on a surface a consumer of @cosyte/dicom reads.
$surface: README.md, TRADEMARKS.md and LICENSE ship in the tarball; docs-content/ is published to docs.cosyte.com; package.json's description and keywords are always scanned. src/ is scanned whole, // comments included, because the published sourcemaps carry every bundled source file in sourcesContent. Two exceptions, each still read by the doc-comment pass: src/dictionary/generated/*.ts, generator output whose string literals are DICOM attribute names the shared phase rule would misread (Phase Encoding Steps), and src/dataset/vr/charset.ts, whose functional NUL byte the surface pass refuses; the source passes read a NUL as a space, so its doc comments and string literals are still scanned. CHANGELOG.md is accounted for, not scanned: it is where item identifiers belong.
$extraRules: dicom's own rules, kept beside the shared ones so the gate reads at least what the former scripts/check-no-internal-refs.ts read: a bare umbrella id (S0228), a bare issue number (#51), any WORD-N id outside the standards and example-value prefixes (TOL-03, never CP-246, MRN-42 or OBR-18), plan decision and threat ids (D-45, T-02-03-01), plan and backlog citations, the ADR, phase, wave, meta-repo and process forms the shared rules narrowed, and a section sign with no PS3.x, Part, Annex, Table, RFC, ISO, IEC or CP context before it on the same line. The negatives are the DICOM reference corpus every rule must leave alone.
